name: UPSC Engineering Services (IES)
description: Technical leadership across Indian Railways, Central Engineering Services, Defense, Power, and Telecommunications. Manage macro infrastructure, border connectivity, and national technical assets.

content_blocks.title: UPSC Engineering Services Examination (ESE/IES) — Master Architecture

content.kicker: UNION PUBLIC SERVICE COMMISSION · ENGINEERING SERVICES (ESE/IES)
content.subtitle: Combined 3-Stage Engineering Merit Blueprint (1,300 Marks Total)
content.description: End-to-end architectural blueprint of the UPSC Engineering Services Examination (ESE/IES). Unlike Civil Services (CSE), Stage 01 (Prelims) marks are cumulative and carried directly forward into the final grand merit tally of 1,300 marks across written papers and the personality interview.

content.dim_note: Cumulative Merit Structure · Every Stage Determines Final Service Allotment

content.description: Administered in OMR objective mode across two sessions on a single day. CRITICAL DISTINCTION: Unlike the Civil Services Examination, marks obtained in ESE Stage 01 are NOT discarded; they contribute 38.5% to the final All-India rank ledger.

papers.name: General Studies & Engineering Aptitude
papers.desc: Tests holistic technical awareness, ethical responsibility, environmental stewardship, project management, and information technologies.
topics: Current issues of national and international importance relating to socio-economic development
Engineering Aptitude covering Logical Reasoning, Analytical Ability, and Spatial Visualization
Engineering Mathematics (Linear Algebra, Calculus, Differential Equations, Numerical Methods)
General Principles of Design, Drawing, and Importance of Safety
Standards and Quality practices in production, construction, maintenance and services
Basics of Energy and Environment: Conservation, pollution control, Climate Change, EIA
Project Management basics, Information and Communication Technologies (ICT), and Ethics

papers.name: Engineering Discipline Objective Paper
papers.desc: Deep technical objective test in the chosen engineering discipline: Civil, Mechanical, Electrical, or Electronics & Telecommunications.
topics: Comprehensive coverage of undergraduate engineering curriculum across all core subjects
Theoretical principles, formula derivations, and standard empirical relationships
High-speed numerical problem solving without calculator assistance
Standard codes of practice (IS / IEC / ASME / IEEE guidelines)
Material science, structural analysis, circuit theory, and thermodynamics

callout.title: Cumulative Scoring & Negative Marking Warning
callout.text: Every incorrect answer incurs a deduction of 1/3rd (-33.33%) of the assigned marks. Because Stage 01 marks are carried forward into the final rank list, candidates cannot treat Prelims as a mere pass/fail threshold. A lead of 40–50 marks in Stage 01 often proves insurmountable in the final service allotment.

content.badge: 4 CORE ENGINEERING STREAMS · UPSC STATUTORY NOTICE
content.warning: Candidates must hold a recognized Engineering Degree (B.E. / B.Tech) or pass Sections A & B of the Institution Examinations (AMIE) in the appropriate discipline.

cards.title: Civil Engineering Cadres
cards.description: Indian Railway Management Service (IRMS-Civil), Central Public Works Department (CPWD), Military Engineer Services (MES), Border Roads Organisation (BRO).

cards.title: Mechanical Engineering Cadres
cards.description: Indian Railway Management Service (IRMS-Mech), Indian Defense Service of Engineers (IDSE), Geological Survey of India, Central Water Engineering Service.

cards.title: Electrical Engineering Cadres
cards.description: IRMS-Electrical, Central Power Engineering Service (CPES), Military Engineer Services, Indian Naval Armament Service (INAS).

cards.title: Electronics & Telecom Cadres
cards.description: Indian Radio Regulatory Service, Indian Telecommunication Service (ITS), Wireless Planning and Coordination, Defense Aeronautical Quality Assurance.

content.description: Two 3-hour subjective written papers in the candidate chosen engineering discipline. Tests analytical derivations, numerical proofs, structural design problems, and technical drawing standards. Non-programmable scientific calculators are permitted.

papers.name: Discipline Technical Paper I
papers.desc: Tests fundamental physical principles, foundational equations, analytical proofs, and structural calculations.
topics: Civil: Building Materials, Solid Mechanics, Structural Analysis, Steel & Concrete Design
Mechanical: Thermodynamics, Fluid Mechanics, Heat Transfer, IC Engines & Power Plant
Electrical: Circuit Analysis, Electromagnetic Fields, Electrical Materials, Measurements & Instrumentation
Electronics: Basic Electronics, Analog & Digital Circuits, Materials & Components, Signals & Systems

papers.name: Discipline Technical Paper II
papers.desc: Advanced systems, applied field engineering, environmental systems, telecommunications, and digital control.
topics: Civil: Geotechnical Engineering, Water Resources, Environmental Engineering, Transportation & Surveying
Mechanical: Theory of Machines, Machine Design, Manufacturing & Industrial Engineering
Electrical: Control Systems, Electrical Machines, Power Systems, Power Electronics & Drives
Electronics: Network Protocols, Control Systems, Communications Engineering, Computer Architecture

callout.title: Conventional Answer Architecture & Step-Marking
callout.text: UPSC awards marks for step-by-step mathematical reasoning, stated assumptions, free-body diagrams, and explicit units. Neatly labeled sketches with standard engineering notations receive substantial bonus consideration compared to raw numerical answers without intermediate work.

content_blocks.title: Stage 03 — Personality Test & Final Technical Ledger (200 Marks)

content.description: The culminating stage conducted at UPSC Headquarters, Dholpur House, New Delhi. An eminent board consisting of UPSC members, senior chief engineers, and technical ministry advisors assesses professional acumen, leadership, and public safety ethics.

papers.name: The ESE Technical Personality Board
papers.meta: 5-Member Board · 30–45 Minutes · UPSC HQ, New Delhi
papers.desc: Evaluates engineering judgment, integrity, handling of public emergencies, knowledge of national infrastructure initiatives, and field project management.
topics: Technical problem solving on practical engineering dilemmas (e.g. bridge collapse, power grid failure)
Knowledge of National Infrastructure Pipeline (NIP), Gati Shakti, and smart governance programs
Leadership composure, moral integrity, public safety ethics, and contract transparency
DAF scrutiny: engineering final-year project, industrial training, and cadre preferences

papers.name: All-India Merit Ledger & Service Allocation
papers.desc: Rank determination across the four engineering disciplines for gazetted Group A appointments under the Government of India.
topics: Civil Engineering: Top ranks allocated to IRMS-Civil, CPWD, and Military Engineer Services
Mechanical Engineering: Allotments across IRMS-Mech, IDSE, and Central Water Engineering
Electrical Engineering: Cadres in IRMS-Elec, CPES, and Naval Armament Service
Electronics & Telecom: Allotments to Indian Telecommunication Service (ITS) and Radio Regulatory

callout.title: Service Allotment & Cadre Seniority
callout.text: Final service preference and cadre allocation are determined strictly by the 1,300-mark cumulative tally. Top scorers secure first-choice services such as IRMS and CPWD, granting immediate executive authority as Assistant Executive Engineers (AEE) in Junior Time Scale.

prerequisites: Nationality: Must be a citizen of India, subject of Nepal/Bhutan, or eligible Tibetan refugee.
Educational Qualification: Degree in Engineering (B.E. / B.Tech) from a recognized University, or passed Sections A & B of the Institution Examinations of the Institution of Engineers (India).
Age Limit (as of 1st January of examination year): 21 to 30 years (relaxable up to 35 for SC/ST, 33 for OBC, and up to 35 for departmental candidates).
Physical Fitness: Candidates must pass the rigorous medical fitness examination as per the Regulations for Physical Examination of Candidates.

roadmap.title: Undergraduate Core Mastery & Engineering Mathematics
roadmap.description: Master core engineering subjects from standard textbooks and complete engineering mathematics and general aptitude.

roadmap.title: Stage 01 Objective Question Practice & Formula Fluency
roadmap.description: Solve past 15 years ESE Prelims papers and build speed solving objective MCQs without a calculator.

roadmap.title: General Studies & Engineering Aptitude Synthesis
roadmap.description: Study energy and environment, safety standards, project management, ethics, and current technical developments.

roadmap.title: Stage 02 Conventional Numerical Derivation & Design Problems
roadmap.description: Practice step-by-step answer writing with non-programmable scientific calculators adhering to IS/IEC codes.

roadmap.title: Full-Length Simulation Regimen (Prelims & Mains Mocks)
roadmap.description: Simulate back-to-back testing days to build physical stamina, mental clarity, and calculation speed.

roadmap.title: DAF Technical Defense & Dholpur House Mock Panels
roadmap.description: Scrub project details in DAF, review national infrastructure initiatives, and attend mock interview panels.

metrics.entry_threshold: B.E. / B.Tech in Civil, Mech, Elec, or E&T
